Python · Tier A

Expose the Controller memory authority and its lifecycle/conflict types.

Responsibilities

Keep the package import surface for the hub, phases and failures.

Boundaries

Importing this package neither acquires ownership nor installs repositories; application startup uses lifecycle and bootstrap to assemble the complete Server graph.

Lifecycle

Consumers import these names before constructing or receiving their hub.

State

No package-level owner or repository is created; each hub instance owns its state.

Security

StateUnavailable and RevisionConflict let callers reject unavailable ownership or stale writes without treating a failed transaction as committed.

Collaborators

hub defines the exported objects; lifecycle manages Server/offline use.

Public surface

src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/bootstrap.py

Python · Tier A

Install the complete Server repository graph in its bootstrap-owned memory hub.

Responsibilities

Construct first-party repositories against one hub, bind redaction and notification settings providers, restore operator targets and fence legacy profiles.

Boundaries

Canonical database paths identify recovery adapters. HTTP service assembly, worker startup and transition to READY remain with the application lifecycle.

Lifecycle

install runs during BOOTSTRAPPING after path ownership/recovery setup; it validates the installed domain set against SERVER_DOMAINS before returning the hub.

State

Repositories register with the supplied hub; existing factories for their paths resolve to that authority. No second default hub is constructed here.

Security

Settings callbacks retain the owning store; target enrollment/profile fences are installed before execution may resume. A domain mismatch fails startup closed.

Collaborators

lifecycle establishes recovery access; native target_identity restores target evidence; each store supplies its own bootstrap and recovery adapter.

Public surface

SERVER_DOMAINS names the required graph; install returns the populated hub or propagates bootstrap/ownership failures without starting service threads.

src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/bootstrap_heap.py

Python · Tier A

Share one process-owned startup GC freeze across embedded Controllers.

Responsibilities

Collect unreachable startup cycles once, freeze surviving bootstrap objects, and unfreeze after the final retaining Controller closes.

Boundaries

Reference counting and collection of new objects remain enabled. Existing embedding-app freeze/disabled-GC policy wins; later request heaps are never captured.

Lifecycle

Capture precedes READY and follows SQLite sealing for application hubs. Subsequent owners retain the same capture; a hub close callback releases its epoch.

State

A process ID, reentrant lock and epoch set fence shared ownership and reentrant collection. Surviving startup cycles can remain until the final owner closes.

Security

Fork children cannot claim or release the parent's freeze; the SQLite scan may omit frozen objects only when this process owns the already-sealed capture.

Collaborators

hub runs close callbacks; sqlite_guard seals bootstrap handles and consults owns_frozen_heap/thaw_interpreter_heap; memory usage reports the retained objects in RSS.

Public surface

retain_bootstrap_heap conditionally captures/retains the heap; owns_frozen_heap reports this process's ownership without initiating collection; thaw_interpreter_heap exposes an interpreter-only permanent generation.

@see src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/hub.py

@see src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/sqlite_guard.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
thaw_interpreter_heap 56 Thaw a permanent generation that holds only the interpreter's immortal objects. CPython 3.12+ moves its immortal objects into the permanent generation during collection, before any application code runs, and moves them back after the next full collection. Exposing them changes no caller's policy and hides no SQLite handle, so any source or compiled Server may do it. Return False, with the generation frozen again, when it holds anything else: those objects belong to an embedding application.

Unsupported/forked/externally frozen GC contexts are left untouched. Repeat calls for the same epoch are idempotent; another active owner shares the original capture rather than freezing request data.

src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/checkpoint.py

Python · Tier A

Persist complete immutable Controller generations through one manifest commit.

Responsibilities

Restore private copies of legacy/committed databases, stage coherent domain snapshots and managed bodies, validate hashes, publish a durable manifest and report checkpoint health without making request paths wait for SQLite or filesystem I/O.

Boundaries

Canonical legacy files are retired after a verified checkpoint replaces them. Only the selected manifest defines recovery truth. Volatile changes have no zero-RPO or exactly-once guarantee; uncertain execution recovery remains with domain owners.

Lifecycle

Adapters register decoded bootstrap state. A READY hub gets one coordinator; its worker coalesces periodic/manual requests, retries failures with bounded backoff, and attempts a snapshot after quiescing before releasing shutdown ownership.

State

The writer lock spans serialization/I/O; a separate status lock serves health reads. Verified immutable domain files may be reused across restarts. One committed generation and one temporary replacement are allowed; publication retires the old save.

Security

Exclusive private files, path/symlink checks, checksums and SQLite integrity validation fence recovery data. Corrupt committed generations fail closed. Diagnostics publish exception types rather than SQL, paths or secret-bearing exception messages.

Collaborators

hub captures/acknowledges revisions; sqlite_guard grants scoped recovery access; managed_files retains bodies; writer_budget paces off-path serialization.

Public surface

SQLiteRepositoryAdapter supplies schema/load/write recovery hooks; CheckpointCoordinator owns flush/request/start/stop/health. Manifest/file helpers are shared with offline generation inspection and copying.

@see src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/hub.py

@see src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/managed_files.py

@see src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/operator.py

src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/contention.py

Python · Tier A

Coordinate overlapping Controller publications when optimistic preparation repeatedly conflicts. PublicationQueue grants expiring dependency reservations without blocking disjoint publishers or immutable snapshot readers; atomic recomputes pure callbacks and publishes only with current revisions and live permission. ContentionDiagnostics retains bounded conflict facts rather than request values. Queue closure or expiry revokes grants without forcibly interrupting callbacks.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation

PublicationQueue.request 71 Append a dependency reservation with increasing FIFO order and a deadline relative to monotonic time. Wake waiters; actual permission is obtained separately by acquire and revalidated at publication.
PublicationQueue.acquire 82 Wait until no granted/earlier overlapping reservation or active publisher covers these keys. Run the caller's lifecycle check, expire leases and use bounded condition waits. Disjoint requests proceed independently; closed, removed or expired tickets raise ReservationExpired.

Reserved publication must stay within its live dependency grant; ordinary publishers wait behind overlapping pending reservations. Always remove the permit on exit. Closing clears reservations but leaves final lifecycle admission to the supplied check.

src/agent_runtime/runtime_state/conversation_retention.py
